memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel went up and saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a pavement made of lapis lazuli, as bright blue as the sky." - Exodus 24:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What an astonishing moment. Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders go up the mountain and see the God of Israel. Scripture does not describe His form — only what lay beneath His feet, a pavement gleaming like sapphire, as clear and blue as the sky itself. The description is deliberately restrained. They saw something of God's glory, though no one can see Him in His full essence and live (Exod 33:20; John 1:18).

Notice what fills the account: beauty, clarity, brilliance. Not terror, not darkness, but a shining pavement like the bright heavens. God's glory is not merely fearsome; it is breathtakingly beautiful. Those who came near did not describe horror but splendour. Our God is glorious in a way that draws the heart even as it humbles it.

And here is the wonder for us: what these seventy-four men glimpsed on a mountain, we have seen far more fully in the face of Jesus Christ. John writes that the Word became flesh and "we have seen his glory" (John 1:14). In Christ, God's glory came near enough to touch, to follow, to know. And one day we will see Him face to face (1 John 3:2). Let your heart be drawn today not only to God's power, but to His beauty.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I see God as beautiful and glorious, or only as powerful and demanding?
How has God revealed His glory to me through Jesus?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are glorious beyond words, and in Jesus I have seen Your beauty. Draw my heart to worship not only Your power but Your splendour, until I see You face to face. Amen.
